subject: Re: TidalTech MSA redlines - notice SLA, defend vs. royalties
messages:
From: Sara Hughes <sara.hughes@tidaltech.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@tidaltech.com, legal@tidaltech.com
Date: 2028-07-29T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: TidalTech MSA redlines (IP / notice SLA / royalties)

Soojin — attaching our marked-up MSA. High level: legal is pushing for a 48-hour notice SLA for any alleged third-party IP claim and wants a carveout ensuring we reimburse royalties for any damages tied to output-derived infringement rather than requiring Redwood to assume defense control for certain categories (third-party content claims, downstream royalties). Procurement is looped since these terms affect budgeting and insurance.

Key asks from TidalTech: 
- 48-hour notice provision and 7-day evidence preservation window (we preserve chains, logs)
- If infringement arises from customer-provided prompts/training data, they want a royalty pathway instead of Redwood taking defense control
- Broad indemnity for customer-facing claims with a carveout for model-training datasets (they propose a shared-liability split)

Can you confirm Redwood's position and whether we can offer a limited royalty remedy as an alternative to defend-and-indemnify for that narrow bucket? Attaching our redlines: TidalTech_MSA_redlines_20280729.docx

Sara
Senior Counsel, TidalTech

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Hughes <sara.hughes@tidaltech.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-29T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TidalTech MSA redlines (IP / notice SLA / royalties)

Sara — thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. Quick read-through notes below; internal team copied. We understand the sensitivity around royalties and chains of custody; want to find a commercial compromise that doesn't expose Redwood to open-ended downstream royalties.

Preliminary stance: 
- Notice SLA: 48 hours is tight operationally; legal operations recommends 72 hours with an agreed escalation ladder (48-hour triage, 72-hour formal notice). We can accept an evidence preservation window of 7 days for immediate triage artifacts and 90 days for forensic artifacts (longer on a case-by-case basis).
- Defend vs. royalty: we are open to discussing a limited royalty remediation if the claim is demonstrably caused by customer-supplied internal dataset or prompt corpus (narrow definition). However, royalty percentages and caps need to be contractually bounded (suggest cap tied to order form value and a per-claim cap).
- Insurance and offsets: Redwood will propose using vendor insurance to cover defense costs first and allow a royalty carveout only where insurance doesn't apply.

Kimberly / Naomi — can legal ops create a short strawman (one page) showing 3 options (Redwood defense; royalty with cap; hybrid — defend for first X, royalty thereafter) we can send to TidalTech this afternoon? Ben — heads-up this will impact pricing if we offer royalty remediation.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TidalTech MSA redlines (IP / notice SLA / royalties)

All — drafting the strawman now. Outline: 
1) SLA/notice: accept 72-hour formal notice, require initial triage acknowledgement within 48 hours; 7-day preservation for ephemeral logs, 90-day for full forensic artifacts tied to order form access.
2) Remediation options: 
   a) Redwood defense control (default) with standard cooperation obligations.
   b) Limited royalty remediation (only where claimant ties infringement to customer-supplied training corpus or prompt-engineered outputs) — royalty limited to 1x annual spend on Redwood services or $250k per claim, whichever is lower.
   c) Hybrid: Redwood defends for first 60 days then parties may elect royalty fallback subject to mutual audit.
3) Insurance waterfall: require TidalTech to exhaust commercial general liability/tech E&O for first-dollar coverage where applicable; Redwood's insurance will not be invoked for customer-caused claims unless agreed.

I will attach the one-pager and a redline excerpt for the IP section. Also adding an evidence-preservation checklist (see attachment). Will need legal sign-off on caps. Naomi — can you run quick actuarial check with finance on the $250k per-claim cap vs. 1x annual spend metric?

Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Hughes <sara.hughes@tidaltech.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-29T12:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TidalTech MSA redlines (IP / notice SLA / royalties)

Sara — appreciate the clarity. Commercial view: if Redwood offers a limited royalty option as Kimberly outlined we will need to reflect this in the order form pricing (either a risk premium or a separate escrow/holdback mechanism). Two practical suggestions: 
- Option 1 (preferred by sales): add a 10% risk surcharge to the order value for customers electing the royalty fallback; this keeps pricing simple and predictable.
- Option 2: establish a refundable escrow equal to 25% of the annual contract value held until the first 12 months lapse without a claim.

Both options are feasible; happy to discuss TidalTech's procurement preference. If they insist on no commercial adjustment, we need tighter definitions and a stricter cap.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Hughes <sara.hughes@tidaltech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@tidaltech.com, legal@tidaltech.com
Date: 2028-07-29T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TidalTech MSA redlines (IP / notice SLA / royalties)

Thanks all — this is helpful. Procurement prefers Option 1 (risk surcharge) to an escrow. Legal will review Kimberly's strawman and the royalty cap; they asked us to propose an alternative cap tied to revenue generated by the infringing outputs (we pushed back and will accept Redwood's $250k suggestion as a starting negotiation point).

Next steps: Kimberly/legal to circulate the one-pager + redline excerpt and evidence checklist. Procurement to confirm whether the 10% surcharge is acceptable (I will route internally). We should aim to finalize a mutual path by EOD Friday July 31 so procurement can sign off.

Sara
Senior Counsel, TidalTech
